<notes>
kept|revised|dropped -> base harness -> base1, base2, base3 diverge on C(80,12) computation (73 vs 47 vs 86 from identical prompts and harness), indicating the LLM narration of tool output is unreliable; this is a real property of the base harness (failure repeats across 3/3)

kept|revised|dropped -> inv1 → extracted C(n,k) from question using regex and computed deterministically with math.comb; rollout produced consistent output (37) without LLM involvement (0 steps, 0 tokens); generalizable pattern that handles arbitrary C(n,k) questions and falls back to LLM only for non-matching questions; the mechanism (deterministic extraction + direct computation) directly addresses the divergence in base set

dropped|excluded|why -> inv2, inv3, dom1, dom2, dom3 → inv2 is equivalent to inv3 (both call tools.python with hardcoded computation, no generalizability); inv3 is simpler than inv2 but less general than inv1; dom1 is deterministic but hardcoded to C(80,12) with no fallback; dom2 is more expensive (LLM call + verification overhead) and still carries LLM dependency; dom3 adds prose to task.md (expensive) and adds number-extraction logic that inv1 does not need (inv1 already returns just the number); inv1 subsumes the benefits of all others at lower cost

checked|held|verified -> no FILE block changes for prompts/system.md, prompts/task.md - inv1 uses base versions unchanged (same placeholders, same content)

checked|verified|safe -> inv1 harness.py preserves interface solve(question, llm, tools, files) -> str, compiles cleanly (imports comb, re from stdlib), all files loaded by code (prompts loaded in fallback path)
</notes>

ADOPT: inv1
